title: Beijing's Famous Dragon Wall? The Real One's in Datong | China Travel Expert
description:
Everyone photographs Beijing's Nine-Dragon Wall. The oldest and biggest one isn't in Beijing at all — it's in Datong, Shanxi.

Datong's Nine-Dragon Wall (九龙壁) was built around 1392 in front of the residence of Zhu Gui, the Prince of Dai and thirteenth son of the first Ming emperor. It runs about 45.5 metres long and 8 metres high — the oldest and largest glazed Nine-Dragon screen still standing in China. Beijing's famous Beihai wall came much later, in 1756, and is only about 25.5 metres long. So the "original" is roughly 360 years older and nearly twice the length.

★ Expert Tip: The wall sits in Datong's old town — pair it with the Huayan Monastery and Shanhua Temple for a half-day of Liao- and Ming-era architecture.

北京的九龙壁最出名，但中国现存最大、最老的九龙壁在山西大同：约1392年为代王朱桂而建，长约45.5米、高约8米，比北京北海1756年的九龙壁早约360年。
